texts.text: Configure the app, the connection and permissions
Screen size sent to the TFT
Shows saved HUD name. Link and video start only by pressing Start.
Rebuilds Wi-Fi Direct automatically and shows name. Video starts only by pressing Start.
Rebuilds link and also starts video. Android still requests screen capture consent.
How many minutes the app actively tries to reconnect to the TFT. Beyond that it switches to passive listening: no attempts, but reconnection still happens automatically when the TFT returns.
Shows HUD, status, IP and link event at the top of Home. Default: hidden.
On startup the app waits and connects by itself as soon as it finds the TFT. If disabled, connection starts from the button on Home.
Short vibration when the TFT link connects or is lost. Useful with the phone in your pocket.
Sets the TFT clock sync packets to fix time issues. Default 3 packets: increase if your TFT resets the time.
View live events and configure file log saving.
Required for the Wi-Fi Direct link and for automatic reconnection while the app is in background.
All good: automatic reconnection works in background too.
Required: Android needs it for the Wi-Fi Direct APIs.
Must be ON: with location off Android refuses to look for the TFT.
Needed for the mirroring service notification.
Exclude the app so reconnection is not frozen.
Used by the START button shown over the app when the TFT is not connected.
Master switch: when OFF the app never uses Shizuku.
Shizuku not active: tap to enable
Needed to change and restore the screen size.
Ready: Shizuku is no longer needed.
Prepare MotoBit first: it is needed only once.
Lowers brightness: the screen stays on
When on, the screen is dimmed and set to the dashboard format
Removes the navigation bar from the video: that space is wasted on the TFT anyway. Optional, can be turned off.
Apply is locked until the restore gestures are active (volume keys and power button). This prevents making the phone unusable again.
The resolution is applied by the bubble, or by covering the sensor in pocket mode.
This phone cannot turn the screen off with the sensor (mode unavailable)
MotoBit needs a small helper to change the screen size. You do it once: after that it is no longer needed.
Keep Shizuku installed: after the setup it is no longer needed, but it is the backup if the permissions are ever lost.
Open the Play Store, search for Shizuku and tap Install. When it is done, come back here.
Open Settings, tap About phone, then tap Build number seven times. You will see You are now a developer. If not, tap again.
Go back, open System then Developer options, and turn on Wireless debugging. Keep Wi-Fi on.
Open Shizuku and tap Start. Choose Pair with code: a notification shows six numbers. Type them in Shizuku and tap Pair.
Tap Start again. Shizuku must show Running.
Open MotoBit, go to Settings, then Permissions, tap Shizuku and then Authorize. Choose Allow.
Still in Permissions, tap Prepare now and wait for Ready. After this, Shizuku is no longer needed.
Pick a percentage: higher means finer text on the dashboard.
Tap the bubble or cover the sensor to apply.
If something is wrong, switch the screen off and on with the power button: everything goes back.
Shizuku does not start: repeat step 4 (pair with code), then step 5.
Permissions say Start Shizuku first: open Shizuku, tap Start and come back here.
The resolution is not applied: open Shizuku, tap Start, then in Permissions tap Prepare now.
You changed phone or cleared MotoBit data: do everything again from the start.
Percentage, dimming, rotation and nav bar will be available in the next phase.
Writes the full log (channels, session, protocol) to the app's Documents folder.
With switch active, full log is written to file in Documents; with switch off, file writing is disabled.
Clock push NOT requested by the TFT on the control socket. Measured that the TFT does not read it: it stays queued and blocks ACKs, making the TFT close the session. Leave OFF.
